aliases: Camellia sinensis var. sinensis cv. Shuchazao
processing: A cultivar used for several teas rather than one finished tea. It suits green tea methods better than yellow ones in comparative work, and has also been made into Qimen-style black tea.
harvest_season: As with Anhui greens in general, spring picking is the prized one; the name's zao means early.
appearance_dry: Depends on the tea; in Shucheng Xiaolanhua it gives loose, naturally opened green strands.
appearance_liquor: As a green tea, pale yellow-green and clear.
appearance_wet: As a green tea, soft green buds and young leaves.
taste_profile: Rich in amino acids and caffeine by analysis, which points to a savoury, fresh cup; the result depends strongly on the style made.

brewing.notes: General advice for an Anhui green. If the leaf has been made into a black tea, use hotter water.

vintage_note: Rarely a label on its own: it reaches drinkers inside named teas such as Shucheng Xiaolanhua, which are sold as the current spring harvest and best drunk within a year.
description:
Shuchazao is one of the working cultivars of Anhui green tea, a plant variety rather than a tea style. It is a selected national-level cultivar tied to the Shucheng Xiaolanhua area, and the 'Shu' in its name matches that county.

Researchers like it, and it turns up all over tea science: experiments on how shading drives theanine in the plant, and on how different cultivars suit different teas. In a study on Huoshan tea, it did better with green tea methods while the local Jinjizhong suited yellow tea methods.

Its chemistry is the interesting part. In a Qimen-style black tea comparison it had less ester catechin and more caffeine and free amino acids than Fuzao 2, for a richer, fresher cup.

You will seldom buy it by name, so read it as a detail about a tea that is sold under a place name. Brew it to the style in the cup. It has also been trialled outside Anhui, including southern Shaanxi, where it made an initial shortlist of clonal cultivars.
history:
Shuchazao is described as a selection made from local population plants and recognised as a national-level cultivar; its year of release and exact breeder are little documented in general references.

It has been trialled outside Anhui and appears often as a research cultivar.
